newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Hock Hua unit stake sold.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Hock Hua unit stake sold.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, May 7 - Following is a selection of analysts' views on the sale of a 51.8 percent stake in the Sabah unit of Hock Hua Bank Bhd for 190 million ringgit to unlisted Malaysian firm Langkah Bahagia Sdn Bhd.
CHAN WEE LEE, BANKING ANALYST AT JUPITER SECURITIES:
"For Hock Hua it's a good thing because obviously on its own it won't meet the Tier-1 status anytime soon.
On a very rough calculation, a banking icence is worth about 250 million ringgit, and 30 to 40 percent above that if it is listed.
So the deal's price is about right. It's a pretty good price to pay for a banking licence.
UCM (Industrial Corp Bhd of which Langkah Bahagia director Mohd Nasir Ali is a director and which has a stockbroking arm) wanted to get the banking licence.
Indications are that they are trying to create a small- to medium-sized financial company."
STEPHEN WELLER, DIRECTOR OF STRATEGY AT PESAKA JARDINE FLEMING:

"The medium- to small-scale banking Industry is coming under increasing pressure to reorganise and consolidate, which equals economies of scale. There is a commercial logic to merging. The central bank is keen to see this happen."
AMIN ABDUL MANAP, SENIOR ANALYST AT MOHAIYANI RESEARCH:
"It's rare for a bank to raise its paid-up capital to one billion instead of the shareholders' funds.
I think it's one of the conditions for the take over (to raise the bank's size).
I think they might inject it into a listed vehicle -- it could be UCM.
The aftermath: probably Daim (Zainuddin, the government's economic adviser involved in the deal) will do something with the bank, probably a merger."
